title: Multiregional Multilingual Eval Runbook and Annotation Charter
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document defines Redwood's standard runbook and annotation charter for running production-grade multilingual evaluations across regions (NA / EU / APAC). It covers dataset design, stratified sampling by locale and intent, annotation workflows and quality gates, benchmark definitions and SLOs, integration points with the eval harness, and how results feed into model-onboarding and regression triage. The goal is to produce repeatable, auditable multilingual benchmarks that surface regressions early and guide quantization and rollout decisions.

Scope

- Languages and locales: initially English (en-US, en-GB), Spanish (es-ES, es-MX), French (fr-FR), Japanese (ja-JP), Korean (ko-KR), and simplified Chinese (zh-CN).
- Workloads: single-turn instruction-following, multi-turn chat, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prompts, and short-form summarization.
- Deployment modes: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC).
- Excluded: multimodal image tasks (handled by separate multimodal evaluation charter).

Goals and success criteria

- Coverage: Each language-locale pair must have at least three distinct prompt strata (information request, instruction transformation, conversational turn-handling).
- Sensitivity: Benchmarks must detect a 2-3% absolute drop in correctness/utility metrics for high-frequency slices and 5% for long-tail slices.
- Turnaround: From triggered run to triageable report < 48 hours for critical slices.
- Traceability: Each evaluated sample must be provenance-tagged with region, model commit, quant-profile, and routing policy.

Roles and ownership

- Owner: Applied ML Platform (engineering) — overall charter and runbook maintenance.
- Steward: Prompt Catalog team — sample curation and prompt taxonomy.
- Annotation Lead: Localization & Labeling (contract-managed) — annotator training and QC.
- Oncall Evals: Two engineers from Eval Harness (rota) — run orchestration, failure triage.
- Incident Escalation: Eng-SRE and Model Onboarding leads for infra or data regressions.

Sampling and dataset construction

1) Population sources:
   - Prod traffic mirrors (privacy filtered) — preferred for high-fidelity slices.
   - Synthetic probe generator (coverage for rare intents).
   - Public corpora (license-checked) for domain diversity.

2) Stratified sampling matrix (example):

| Slice | Fraction | Minimum samples per locale | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| High-frequency API intents (top 20) | 40% | 1,000 | Derived from token-level telemetry |
| Medium-frequency conversational flows | 30% | 500 | Includes multi-turn context length variance |
| Long-tail and adversarial probes | 20% | 200 | Synthesized/perturbed examples |
| Edge case regulatory/legal queries | 10% | 100 | Hand-curated by compliance |

3) Locale balancing:
   - For NA/EU/APAC mirror splits, ensure per-locale minimums are met even if overall sample budget is constrained.

Annotation charter

- Annotator skill requirements:
  - Native or near-native fluency in target locale.
  - Familiarity with LLM behaviors and hallucination patterns.
  - Training completion and passing qualification tests (80%+).

- Annotation schema (flat labels):
  - correctness: {correct, partially_correct, incorrect}
  - hallucination: {none, minor, major}
  - instruction-following: {compliant, off_task, unsafe}
  - fluency: {good, acceptable, poor}
  - safety_flag: {none, potential_harm, definite_harm}

- Annotation instructions (high-level):
  1. Read the prompt and the model response end-to-end; do not use external knowledge beyond common facts unless asked.
  2. Judge correctness relative to the explicit prompt constraints and the expected output spec for the slice.
  3. For multi-turn, evaluate coherence across turns and whether the model preserves context.
  4. Record exact spans for hallucinated facts where possible (free-text field).

Quality control and inter-annotator agreement (IAA)

- Gold sets: 10% of each batch pre-labeled by internal SMEs.
- Dual annotation: 25% of samples annotated by two independent annotators; calculate Cohen’s Kappa per slice. Thresholds: Kappa >= 0.7 for high-frequency slices; 0.6 acceptable for long-tail.
- Adjudication: For disagreements on high-frequency slices or safety flags, escalation to annotation lead and a domain SME.
- Batch acceptance criteria: batch-level accuracy on gold >= 90% and Kappa thresholds met.

Benchmark metrics and SLOs

- Primary metrics (per-slice):
  - Correctness Rate (CR): fraction labeled correct or partially_correct.
  - Hallucination Rate (HR): fraction with hallucination != none.
  - Instruction Compliance (IC): compliant rate.
  - Coherence Score (CS): subjective 1-5 normalized to 0-1.

- Secondary metrics:
  - Latency median (p50) and tail (p99) when run through eval harness with same routing policies.
  - Token cost estimate (per-request) for cost-performance tradeoffs.

- Alerting thresholds (example):
  - CR drop > 2 percentage points (pp) on any high-frequency slice -> priority P1 eval alert.
  - HR increase > 3 pp on safety-sensitive slices -> P0 immediate hold of rollout and notify SRE + Security.
  - IC drop > 5 pp across locale -> P1 investigating for prompt or model drift.

Integration with eval harness and CI/CD

- Triggering:
  - Scheduled nightly runs for full multilingual sweep with reduced sample sizes.
  - On-commit hooks: run smoke subset for changed model commits and quant profiles.
  - Pre-rollout: full-run for canary deployments and quant-transitions.

- Artifacts produced:
  - Per-run CSV with sample id, locale, model_hash, quant_profile, labels, annotator ids.
  - Dashboard snapshot: per-slice metrics with trendlines and provenance tags.
  - Attachments: sample-level diffs between baseline and candidate responses (side-by-side).

- CI gating policy (minimum):
  1. Smoke pass: No P0-level regressions on smoke slices.
  2. Canary pass: No P1 regressions on high-frequency slices after 24-hour canary.
  3. Full-run: Allowed minor degradations limited by a regression budget defined by product owner.

Operational runbook: triage workflow

1) Alert received (automated) -> notify oncall-evals and create triage ticket with link to dashboard.
2) Triage engineer runs quick delta check: compare candidate vs baseline on top 5 impacted slices.
3) If regression correlates with quant_profile or kernel change -> tag as quant-sensitive and notify runtime team.
4) If regression correlates with prompt-space change -> notify Prompt Catalog and Product.
5) If safety_flag triggered -> immediate rollback to last passing commit and notify Security.
6) Root cause analysis timeline: initial findings within 8 hours, full RCA within 72 hours.

Dataset lifecycle and retirement

- Versioning: Each prompt set and annotation snapshot must be versioned in the prompt catalog with semantic versioning vMAJOR.MINOR.patch.
- Retirement criteria: A prompt slice may be retired if:
  - It has < 0.01% real-world occurrence over trailing 90 days AND
  - It consistently shows high annotator agreement (Kappa > 0.8) with stable metric behavior for 6 months.
- Archival: Retired slices archived to cold storage with a rationale note and link to historical runs.

Quantization and performance profiling tie-ins

- Each eval run must include metadata on quant_profile used (bits, per-channel scaling, kernel hints).
- For quant-sensitive slices (identified during canary), schedule a dedicated quant-fidelity sweep with increased sample density and SME review.
- Cost-performance notebook: attach model-token-cost estimates and throughput benchmarks to the run artifact for product tradeoff decisions.

Security, privacy and compliance considerations

- PII handling: Samples derived from production traffic must be sanitized using the PII scrubber pipeline before annotation.
- Data residency: Locale-specific samples must remain in-region during annotation where legal/regulatory constraints require.
- Access control: Annotator and reviewer access controlled via RBAC and audit-logged.

Diagnostics, tooling and examples

- CLI snippet: run a locale sweep (example)

  redwood-eval run --suite multilingual_sweep --locales en-US,es-MX,zh-CN --model-hash abc123 --quant q8_asc --output /tmp/run_abc123.csv

- Minimal YAML sample for CI smoke job:

  job: multilingual-smoke
  schedule: nightly
  samples: 200
  locales: [en-US, es-MX, fr-FR]
  metrics: [CR, HR, IC]

Escalation contacts

- Applied ML Platform Pager: #applied-ml-oncall (Slack)
- Eng-SRE: eng-sre-pager@example.com
- Security: security-incident@example.com

Appendix A — Example adjudication template

- Record: sample_id, locale, prompt_text, baseline_response, candidate_response, annotator_x_labelset, annotator_y_labelset, adjudicator_resolution, adjudicator_notes.

Appendix B — Glossary

- Slice: a named partition of workload defined by intent, context-length, and locale.
- Quant profile: model-specific quantization settings used at inference time.
- Canary: a limited rollout configuration used to validate a change in production traffic.
